newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Justice Ministry mulling T-bill tax letter.
newsitem.headline: Russian Justice Ministry mulling T-bill tax letter.

text.p: Russia's Ministry of Justice is still examining a letter from the finance ministry and Federal Tax Service about the implementation of a new tax on government securities and will not approve it before Wednesday, a senior Justice Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"This document, a letter about how to apply the articles of the law on profit tax, is now being examined at the Ministry of Justice," said the official, who asked not to be named.
"It's difficult to say when there will be a result. But of course it won't be approved before tomorrow," the official said.
Federal Tax Service chief spokeswoman Lyudmila Chepakina told Reuters the justice ministry would approve the document on February 1 at the earliest.
President Yeltsin this month approved a new law passed by parliament which imposed the usual profits tax, which is 43 percent for banks and 35 percent for other entities, on government securities.
But interest from bond coupons would be taxed at 15 percent.

The finance ministry and Federal Tax Service wrote to the justice ministry proposing all earnings on government securities, including gains on discount paper, should be classified as interest, like the coupons, and thus eligible for the 15 percent rate.
Government officials had originally envisioned a 15 percent rate for the securities.
The tax will only apply to new securities issued after the tax is implemented.
Because of the uncertainty, the finance ministry last week cancelled an auction of new GKO discount Treasury bills, and issued a new tranche of older paper instead.

At present it is still planning to auction 7.00 trillion roubles of new 273-day T-bills, which would come under the new tax, and a 504-day 4.00 trillion rouble new tranche of an OFZ interest-bearing government bond.
